# M0-S5: when cgo is on, CC is unset, and the default C compiler is
# hidden from PATH, logos and go fall back to zig cc -target <triple>
# if zig is on PATH. The fake zig logs its arguments, strips zig's
# leading "cc -target <triple>", and delegates the rest to the real C
# compiler recorded below before PATH narrows, so the build finishes
# with the same compiler it would otherwise use. The fake and the
# capture need POSIX sh, so this fallback coverage is Unix only
# (see the report for the Windows risk).
# PATH holds the fake-zig directory plus GOROOT/bin: the relative default
# compiler stays hidden while the fake zig and the go tool stay findable.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache

# Install the fake zig, and record the real C compiler before PATH
# narrows; the fake delegates to the recorded path.
chmod 0755 $WORK/fakebin/zig
exists -exec $WORK/fakebin/zig
[!GOOS:windows] exec sh -c 'command -v cc || command -v gcc || command -v clang'
[!GOOS:windows] cp stdout $WORK/realcc.txt
env REALPATH=$PATH

# Case 1: loGo/s module with cgo = "allow". CC unset, default compiler
# hidden, fake zig on PATH: the build falls back to zig and runs.
cd zm
env CC=
env CGO_ENABLED=
env ZIGLOG=$WORK/zig-a.log
env PATH=$WORK/fakebin:$GOROOT/bin
[cgo] logos run .
[cgo] stdout '^zm: 42$'
[cgo] grep 'cc -target' $WORK/zig-a.log
[cgo] [GOOS:linux] [GOARCH:amd64] grep 'cc -target x86_64-linux-musl' $WORK/zig-a.log
cd ..

# Case 2: the same cgo package as a Go module (no logos.toml) with
# CGO_ENABLED=1: the fallback serves Go packages under both commands.
# gb1 and gb2 are identical packages under different paths so neither
# build can hit the other's cache entry and skip the compiler.
cd gm
env CGO_ENABLED=1
env ZIGLOG=$WORK/zig-b-logos.log
[cgo] logos build -o gb1.bin ./gb1
[cgo] grep 'cc -target' $WORK/zig-b-logos.log
[cgo] [GOOS:linux] [GOARCH:amd64] grep 'cc -target x86_64-linux-musl' $WORK/zig-b-logos.log
env ZIGLOG=$WORK/zig-b-go.log
[cgo] go build -o gb2.bin ./gb2
[cgo] grep 'cc -target' $WORK/zig-b-go.log
[cgo] [GOOS:linux] [GOARCH:amd64] grep 'cc -target x86_64-linux-musl' $WORK/zig-b-go.log
cd ..

# Case 3: CGO_ENABLED unset, CC unset, default compiler hidden: cgo
# stays off under both commands even with the fake zig on PATH, so the
# zig log stays empty.
cd gm
env CGO_ENABLED=
env ZIGLOG=$WORK/zig-c.log
[cgo] ! logos build -o gb1.bin ./gb1
[cgo] stderr 'build constraints exclude all Go files'
[cgo] ! go build -o gb1.bin ./gb1
[cgo] stderr 'build constraints exclude all Go files'
[cgo] ! exists $WORK/zig-c.log
cd ..

-- zm/go.mod --
module example.com/zm

go 1.27

-- zm/logos.toml --
[build]
cgo = "allow"

-- zm/main.lgo --
package main

/*
int answer() { return 42; }
*/
import "C"

import "fmt"

func main() { fmt.Println("zm:", C.answer()) }

-- gm/go.mod --
module example.com/gm

go 1.27

-- gm/gb1/main.go --
package main

/*
int answer() { return 42; }
*/
import "C"

import "fmt"

func main() { fmt.Println("gm:", C.answer()) }

-- gm/gb2/main.go --
package main

/*
int answer() { return 42; }
*/
import "C"

import "fmt"

func main() { fmt.Println("gm:", C.answer()) }

-- $WORK/fakebin/zig --
#!/bin/sh
# Fake zig for the M0-S5 zig-fallback attack. It logs zig's argv, strips
# zig's leading "cc -target <triple>", and delegates the remaining C
# compiler arguments to the real C compiler at an absolute path, so the
# build finishes without needing PATH.
echo "zig $@" >>"${ZIGLOG:-$WORK/zig.log}"
if [ "$#" -lt 3 ]; then
	echo "fake zig: expected 'cc -target <triple>' arguments, got: $@" >&2
	exit 1
fi
shift 3
IFS= read -r real <"$WORK/realcc.txt"
if [ -z "$real" ]; then
	echo "fake zig: no pre-narrowing compiler recorded in $WORK/realcc.txt" >&2
	exit 1
fi
PATH=$REALPATH exec "$real" "$@"
